correctness.rationale: Off-diagonal Jacobian entries are exactly twice adjugate entries; the rank-one symmetric adjugate test proves the singular support equals the corank-two locus plus n star spaces. Gram parametrization by n isotropic vectors in dimension n−2≥3 proves the corank-two locus irreducible and gives codimension three; known determinantal degree supplies its degree. Restriction of minors modulo star ideals gives exact scheme intersections. A precise Schur-complement local quadratic form and explicit rank-n−2 kernel witnesses establish two generic transverse ordinary-double-point types. Singular codimension at least two within the irreducible hypersurface proves normality. The standalone checker exhaustively verified the complete size-five Jacobian equivalence over F3 and exact witnesses for sizes 5..12; this finite check is not a substitute for the universal symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant El Maazouz–Sturmfels–Sverrisdóttir rank-variety theorem already implies the corank-two locus degree and irreducibility; these are not claimed novel. The additional n rank-(n−1) star components, their distinct dimensions, scheme-theoretic incidence, and generic quadratic germs were not identified as established in inspected relevant sections or published-finding corpus searches. The full classification is a motivated specialization but could be an implicit corollary of broader work; this is reported as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The explicit hollow determinant Jacobian decomposition may have appeared in older literature under graph adjacency or special symmetroid terminology.

A skilled reader could possibly extract much of the theorem by combining the 2024 general Gram rank results with standard symmetric determinant Jacobian facts; no claim of logical independence from that toolkit is made.
The bibliography was not exhaustive across closed-access or unindexed sources.

value.rationale: The complete reduced singular-support classification is a natural missing geometric invariant of a zero-block symmetric determinant family already known through its rank strata. It detects an entire lower-dimensional set of corank-one singular components invisible to naive corank-two descriptions, determines all their incidence and two transverse quadratic types, and explains connected non-equidimensional singularity. Its precise n≥5 boundary reflects irreducibility of isotropic-cone Gram rank strata and differs from the reducible size-four boundary; the result is not a mere restatement of a degree table.
